meta.title: The formalisation gap
meta.subtitle: 22 classical laws that break at the quantum level (dead ends), six patterns (conjectures), q-number and constructor-theoretic restatements, Lean results (T2).

nodes.title: Newton/Hamilton trajectories
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: action ~ hbar. Replaced by: Schrodinger / Heisenberg.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P2 Joint sharpness, P1 Continuum.

nodes.title: Liouville phase-space density
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: interference states. Replaced by: von Neumann; Wigner can go negative.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P2 Joint sharpness.

nodes.title: Rayleigh-Jeans law
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: h nu >~ k_B T. Replaced by: Planck law.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P1 Continuum.

nodes.title: Equipartition theorem
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: hbar omega >> k_B T. Replaced by: Bose-Einstein mode energy.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P1 Continuum.

nodes.title: Dulong-Petit law
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: low T. Replaced by: Einstein 1907, Debye T^3.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P1 Continuum.

nodes.title: Larmor radiation / classical atom
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: atoms. Replaced by: Bohr, then Schrodinger bound states.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P1 Continuum, P2 Joint sharpness.

nodes.title: Wien/Lenard photoelectric expectation
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: light on metals. Replaced by: E_max = h nu - phi.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P1 Continuum.

nodes.title: Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: n lambda^3 >~ 1. Replaced by: Fermi-Dirac, Bose-Einstein.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P5 Labelled identity.

nodes.title: Gibbs entropy without 1/N!
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: mixing identical gases. Replaced by: symmetrised states.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P5 Labelled identity.

nodes.title: Drude conductivity at low T
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: metals. Replaced by: Sommerfeld/Bloch, BCS.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P5 Labelled identity, P1 Continuum.

nodes.title: Curie law / Bohr-van Leeuwen
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: every magnet. Replaced by: quantised spin and orbital momentum.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P1 Continuum, P2 Joint sharpness.

nodes.title: Classical spin (Stern-Gerlach)
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: inhomogeneous B field. Replaced by: spin-1/2.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P1 Continuum, P2 Joint sharpness.

nodes.title: Classical vacuum (no Casimir)
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: plates ~ um apart. Replaced by: zero-point energy.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P1 Continuum, P2 Joint sharpness.

nodes.title: Fourier heat law at nanoscale
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: below phonon mean free path. Replaced by: phonon Boltzmann transport.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P6 Smooth at all scales, P1 Continuum.

nodes.title: Navier-Stokes at pinch-off/superfluid
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: neck ~ nm; He-II. Replaced by: molecular dynamics; quantised vortices.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P6 Smooth at all scales, P1 Continuum.

nodes.title: Third law vs classical entropy
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: T -> 0. Replaced by: gapped discrete spectrum.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P1 Continuum.

nodes.title: Bell local hidden variables
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: space-like separated entangled pairs. Replaced by: Tsirelson 2 sqrt 2.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P3 Local realism, P2 Joint sharpness.

nodes.title: Classical measurement (no disturbance)
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: non-commuting observables. Replaced by: measurement back-action.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P4 Universal distinguishability and copying, P2 Joint sharpness.

nodes.title: Universal copying of information
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: unknown quantum states. Replaced by: no-cloning; superinformation.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P4 Universal distinguishability and copying.

nodes.title: Classical tunnelling barrier
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: thin barriers, light particles. Replaced by: Gamow tunnelling.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P2 Joint sharpness.

nodes.title: Einstein field equations at Planck scale
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: singularities; l_P. Replaced by: unknown (quantum gravity); BMV tests.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P6 Smooth at all scales, P1 Continuum.

nodes.title: QFT without cutoff (UV divergences)
nodes.statement: Classical law, taken as exact. Fails in regime: short distances. Replaced by: renormalisation; EFT.
nodes.lesson: Failed assumption: P6 Smooth at all scales.

nodes.title: P1 Continuum
nodes.statement: Energy and modes are infinitely divisible. Fails where hbar*omega >~ k_B T, or action ~ hbar.
nodes.test: Find a classical law that fails at the quantum level for a reason not covered by the six patterns; currently 14/22 rows carry this tag.

nodes.title: P2 Joint sharpness
nodes.statement: Every observable has a sharp value at once (phase-space points). Fails because [q,p] = i*hbar.
nodes.test: Find a classical law that fails at the quantum level for a reason not covered by the six patterns; currently 9/22 rows carry this tag.

nodes.title: P3 Local realism
nodes.statement: Correlations come from local pre-set values. Fails because CHSH reaches 2*sqrt(2) > 2.
nodes.test: Find a classical law that fails at the quantum level for a reason not covered by the six patterns; currently 1/22 rows carry this tag.

nodes.title: P4 Universal distinguishability and copying
nodes.statement: Every state can be perfectly distinguished and copied. Fails: non-orthogonal states, no-cloning.
nodes.test: Find a classical law that fails at the quantum level for a reason not covered by the six patterns; currently 2/22 rows carry this tag.

nodes.title: P5 Labelled identity
nodes.statement: Identical particles carry labels. Fails: (anti)symmetrised states, Bose/Fermi statistics.
nodes.test: Find a classical law that fails at the quantum level for a reason not covered by the six patterns; currently 3/22 rows carry this tag.

nodes.title: P6 Smooth at all scales
nodes.statement: A differential (field) description holds down to arbitrarily small scales. Fails: divergences.
nodes.test: Find a classical law that fails at the quantum level for a reason not covered by the six patterns; currently 4/22 rows carry this tag.

nodes.title: Tag counts of the catalogue
nodes.statement: In our tagging: continuum 14, joint sharpness 9, smooth 4, labelled 3, distinguishability 2, local realism 1 (of 22).
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.continuum_most_common. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: No continuum information variable on a finite substrate
nodes.statement: A substrate with finitely many states has no family of non-empty pairwise-disjoint attributes indexed by R.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.no_continuum_info_variable_of_finite. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: Kuypers' droplet (toy)
nodes.statement: Any real-valued quantity on a finite substrate misses every open interval: a finite-atom neck cannot sweep a continuum of radii.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.finite_substrate_misses_interval. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: Overlapping attributes cannot be distinguished
nodes.statement: In the deterministic theory, sending x and y to disjoint outputs is impossible if x and y overlap.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.distinguish_impossible_of_overlap. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: Disjoint attributes can be distinguished
nodes.statement: In the deterministic theory, disjoint x, y with inhabited outputs can be sent to disjoint outputs.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.distinguish_possible_of_disjoint. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: Spin components are q-numbers
nodes.statement: sigma_x sigma_z != sigma_z sigma_x over C (ConstructorTheory/QNumber.lean).
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.pauliX_mul_pauliZ_ne. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: No state is sharp for both sigma_x and sigma_z
nodes.statement: No non-zero vector in C^2 is an eigenvector of both sigma_x and sigma_z (ConstructorTheory/QNumber.lean).
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.no_common_eigenvector. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: Classical copying (CT)
nodes.statement: In the deterministic theory every variable is an information variable: its cloning task is possible (ConstructorTheory/CTRestatement.lean).
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.functional_every_variable_info. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: No superinformation in the deterministic theory
nodes.statement: The deterministic (classical) theory has no superinformation medium; no-cloning and complementarity need non-classical constructors (CTRestatement.lean).
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.functional_no_superinformation. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: Changing a conserved quantity is impossible (toy principle VIII)
nodes.statement: In a toy thermodynamic theory whose constructors conserve U, x -> y and y -> x are both impossible when U differs (CTRestatement.lean).
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.conserved_change_impossible_both. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: Decreasing the monotone is impossible (toy law of impotence)
nodes.statement: In the toy thermodynamic theory, x -> y is impossible when the entropy-like monotone is strictly lower on y (CTRestatement.lean).
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.monotone_decrease_impossible. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: Constructor-based irreversibility (toy)
nodes.statement: A task can be possible while its transpose is impossible (CTRestatement.lean).
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.irreversible_of. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: Irreversibility is not vacuous (two-state example)
nodes.statement: On Bool, false -> true is possible and true -> false impossible in the toy thermodynamic theory (CTRestatement.lean).
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.thermo_irreversible_example. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: Breakdown is exact (Ben's thesis, schema)
nodes.statement: A law that is derived from and entails 'every task in X is possible' fails in a theory iff some task of X is impossible there.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.law_fails_iff. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: FD forbids continuum read-outs
nodes.statement: Under finite distinguishability, no read-out of a continuum of bounded-energy attributes is possible.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.fd_no_continuum_readout. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: FD in a deterministic theory = finite energy shells
nodes.statement: The deterministic theory satisfies FD on S for E iff every shell {E <= e} is finite.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.functional_fd_iff_finite_shells. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: The classical continuum violates FD for every energy function
nodes.statement: For any E : R -> R, the deterministic theory on a line violates FD (a countable union of finite shells cannot cover R).
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.continuum_violates_fd. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: A ladder of quanta satisfies FD
nodes.statement: Levels n with energy n (units of hbar*omega) have finite shells, so FD holds on the ladder.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.ladder_fd. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: No-cloning (Wootters-Zurek/Dieks), any dimension
nodes.statement: An inner-product-preserving map that clones psi and phi onto a normalised blank forces <psi,phi> in {0,1}.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.no_cloning_overlap. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: Cloning non-orthogonal qubit states is an impossible task
nodes.statement: In any isometric two-qubit theory, cloning two states with overlap outside {0,1} is impossible.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.qclone_impossible_of_overlap. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: The computational basis is an information variable (CNOT)
nodes.statement: CNOT clones {|0>, |1>} onto |0>.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.qubit_basis_clone_possible. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: The rotated basis {phi, phi_perp} is an information variable
nodes.statement: (R x R) CNOT (R^H x 1) clones {(3,4)/5, (-4,3)/5} onto |0>.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.qubit_rotated_clone_possible. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: A variable that is not an information variable
nodes.statement: {|0>} and {(3|0>+4|1>)/5} are disjoint, yet cloning them is impossible (overlap 3/5).
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.qubit_nonorthogonal_clone_impossible. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: The classical copying law breaks exactly at a non-orthogonal pair
nodes.statement: In the isometric qubit theory a pair of distinct sharp states cannot be cloned, while the basis can.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.copying_law_breaks_in_qubit. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: The quantum qubit theory is a superinformation theory
nodes.statement: {|0>,|1>} and {phi,phi_perp} are information variables; their union is not (Deutsch-Marletto, cloning clause).
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.qubit_superinformation. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: Equipartition is the ceiling of the Planck factor
nodes.statement: x/(e^x - 1) <= 1 for x > 0: a quantised mode never holds more than k_B T on average.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.planckFactor_le_one. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: High-frequency modes freeze out
nodes.statement: x/(e^x - 1) -> 0 as x -> infinity: the ultraviolet catastrophe is removed.
nodes.note: Lean: ConstructorTheory.tendsto_planckFactor_atTop. Kernel-checked by `lake build` in CI; harness/run_checks.py audits axioms. No human referee yet.

nodes.title: Ben's thesis: the breakdown shows the description is incorrect
nodes.statement: Classical laws are false-but-emergent approximations; the error lives in ontological assumptions encoded in the mathematics (continuum, joint sharpness, unlimited distinguishability), not in the calculus.
nodes.test: Exhibit a classical law whose quantum-level failure is NOT traceable to one of P1-P6 (would refute the 'single root cause' part).

nodes.title: Quantum theory carries the same kind of assumptions
nodes.statement: Continuous Hilbert space, complex amplitudes and smooth spacetime are themselves encoded ontological assumptions; QFT/GR divergences are their failure signal.
nodes.vivid: Kuypers: as atomic theory fixed fluid divergences, a future theory may fix QFT's.

nodes.title: Formalise quantum no-cloning in the task vocabulary
nodes.statement: Prove 'clone every state of a qubit' impossible in a Hilbert-space Theory model (Mathlib inner-product spaces).
nodes.note: Answered in ClosingTheGap.lean: isometric theory, no_cloning_overlap, qubit_superinformation.

nodes.title: C1 Finite distinguishability per action (FD)
nodes.statement: A substrate with energy <= E evolving for time t passes through at most ~2Et/(pi*hbar) perfectly distinguishable states (Margolus-Levitin) and, within radius R, holds at most ~2*pi*R*E/(hbar*c*ln2) bits (Bekenstein). Proposed as a constructor-theoretic principle, not a dynamical theorem.
nodes.test: Any substrate shown to perfectly distinguish more states than the bound allows refutes C1 (and quantum theory with it).

nodes.title: C2 Superinformation + interoperability generate the q-number algebra
nodes.statement: Deutsch-Marletto superinformation plus the reconstruction axioms (Hardy; Chiribella-D'Ariano-Perinotti; Masanes-Mueller) single out complex Hilbert space, hence the q-number forms of the 18 'established' rows.
nodes.test: A consistent superinformation theory that is not quantum and also passes the reconstruction axioms would refute 'generate'.

nodes.title: C3 Quantitative possibility: possible to accuracy eps at cost >= f(eps)
nodes.statement: Attach resource costs to tasks (time, energy, steps) so that rates and coefficients become lower bounds on cost (third law: Masanes-Oppenheim).
nodes.test: A rate or coefficient (e.g. a tunnelling rate) that provably cannot be written as an optimal cost of any task refutes C3 for that row.

nodes.title: C4 Classical law = quantum law + possibility assumption X
nodes.statement: Every catalogue law rests on a class X of tasks that classical physics assumes possible; it fails exactly where X contains an impossible task.
nodes.test: A catalogue law with no such X, or one whose failure lies outside X, refutes C4.

nodes.title: Chosen model: C4 frame with C1 + C2 as the two forbidden-task principles
nodes.statement: Classical laws assume two classes of tasks possible: copying arbitrary states (forbidden by superinformation) and distinguishing unboundedly many states with bounded action (forbidden by FD). Breakdown happens exactly at those tasks.
nodes.test: Find a catalogue row whose breakdown needs neither a forbidden copy nor a forbidden fine distinction (rows 3, 12, 13, 18 are the live candidates).

nodes.title: Derive FD from the Margolus-Levitin bound in Lean
nodes.statement: In a finite-dimensional Hilbert-space Theory, prove that orthogonalisation takes time >= pi*hbar/(2E), so a bounded-energy, bounded-time task distinguishes finitely many states.

nodes.title: CHSH <= 2 for local models, Tsirelson for quantum
nodes.statement: Formalise the classical CHSH bound (finite, decidable) and state the quantum violation.

nodes.title: Equipartition vs discrete modes
nodes.statement: Prove that a discrete mode spectrum gives a finite total mean energy where equipartition diverges (Rayleigh-Jeans vs Planck).
